note: Attacker-controlled raw bytes are passed to libvips as an image buffer; the JPEG loader will parse embedded EXIF segments.
The EXIF blob extracted from the JPEG APP1 segment is handed to libexif with its full size.
libvips calls libexif's loader without applying the EXIF fixup path, so the raw (possibly truncated) buffer is parsed directly.

code: unsigned char *d = data; unsigned int ds = size;
note: Entry point of the vulnerable parser; d points to the heap buffer and ds is its declared size.
The full data size is captured before any later capping; this value is later passed to maker-note parsing.
ds is capped to 0xfffe for the main IFD walk, but fullds retains the original larger size.
Maker-note interpretation is invoked with the uncapped fullds while d points into the actual heap buffer whose real size may be smaller, enabling an out-of-bounds read.
The uncapped size is forwarded to the maker-note loader, which trusts it as the buffer length.
Dispatch to the vendor-specific maker-note parser with the oversized length.

The Canon parser reads 6-byte entries using the inflated buf_size as the bound; when the actual heap allocation is smaller, the 6-byte memcpy reads past the end of the buffer, producing the heap-buffer-overflow READ of 6 bytes.
